description: A numeric DISPLAY literal that is not an unsigned integer (signed, or with a digit position right of the decimal point) — a COBOL-2002 relaxation of a COBOL-85 restriction. §1985:VI.6.10.3 SR2: "If literal-1 is numeric, then it must be an unsigned integer." ISO/IEC 1989:2002 Annex F.2 item 46 names the sign half: "DISPLAY statement. If the literal in a DISPLAY statement is numeric, it may be signed."; the integer half is the 2002 text's own (14.8.10.2 prints no rule on a numeric literal-1, as §2023:14.9.11.3 prints none), so one row answers the one 1985 rule (kb/Work PB5074). COBOL-85 is the edition a 2002 Annex F.2 'formerly' statement describes: the owner's decision of 2026-10-31 (kb/Work PB4305) makes the F.2 statements the rule for the 85 edge, as D-SIGN2 (item 124) and PB3683 (item 123) did; GnuCOBOL -std=cobol85 accepts some of them as dialect leniency, which rule 1 places below the ISO text. Gated in ONE place, VersionConformancePass.ParseArm.VisitDisplayStatement, once per such literal operand (kb/Work PB4305, PB5074; VCR row 7.47).
display: a numeric DISPLAY literal that is not an unsigned integer
